subject: Contract duration & cancellation playbook — addendum request
messages:
From: Leah Morris <leah.morris@acme.com>
To: ben.carter@redwood.com
Cc: Tom Alvarez <t.alvarez@capstonelegal.com>, acmecorp-contracts@acme.com
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood MSA / Order Form — term and cancellation clarification

Hi Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the platform looks promising for our agent-assist rollout. Procurement asked us to confirm a couple of term mechanics before we move the PO through the queue. High level asks:

- Can we get an explicit 60-day cancellation notice window for the Order Form (instead of the 30 days in the draft)?
- Relatedly, we need a mutual termination for convenience (TFC) option on the Order Form (30-60 day) with a narrow list of transition obligations; we want to avoid broad exit fees.

Our legal counsel (Tom) is looped for redlines. I attached the current Order Form PDF for context. Can Redwood propose a short addendum that harmonizes Term + Auto‑Renew + TFC? If possible, include a fallback timeline for data export and a minimal support handoff.

Goal: We want clean language so internal execs can approve without waiting for a deep SOW negotiation. Appreciate a suggested playbook we can align on.

Best,
Leah
Leah Morris
Head of IT Procurement, Acme Corp
leah.morris@acme.com

Attachment: OrderForm_ACME_v3.pdf (pdf, 240KB)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Leah Morris <leah.morris@acme.com>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com, Tom Alvarez <t.alvarez@capstonelegal.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood MSA / Order Form — term and cancellation clarification

Leah — thanks for the clear asks and for sending the Order Form.

High level response: yes, we can accommodate a 60‑day notice option and a mutual TFC on the Order Form. To keep approvals fast, we typically handle these via a one‑page addendum that:

- Overrides the Order Form: sets notice period and TFC timelines (30/60 options)
- Defines a short transition scope (data export formats, retention hold, limited post‑termination support for 30 days)
- Confirms no exit escrow or broad wind‑down fees beyond committed usage for the term

I've asked Legal (Neha) and Sales Ops (Lauren) to propose language and a minimal playbook for the procurement team. Next steps I propose:
1) Redwood shares a draft addendum and a 1‑page playbook (who owns export, typical timelines).
2) Acme reviews and flags any mandatory procurement language (if any).
3) If redlines are minor, we execute via DocuSign. If material, loop in legal counsel for a brief call.

Attaching a starter addendum (Redwood_Term_Addendum_v1.docx) — it contains two options for the notice window and TFC timing: Option A (30 days) and Option B (60 days). Please review and mark up.

Thanks — will expedite on our side.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

Attachment: Redwood_Term_Addendum_v1.docx (docx, 18KB)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: ben.carter@redwood.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, Leah Morris <leah.morris@acme.com>, Tom Alvarez <t.alvarez@capstonelegal.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Sep 2026 09:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood MSA / Order Form — term and cancellation clarification

Looping in a couple of quick points from Legal after an initial pass on the addendum:

- Show both candidate windows but label the 60‑day as "Customer‑requested" — that helps with internal approvals for reserved capacity deals.
- For TFC, we should limit Redwood's post‑termination obligations to: (i) make available self‑service export for 30 days in common formats, (ii) assist with reasonable export troubleshooting for up to 15 hours, and (iii) honor data retention hold for logs for 90 days if requested in writing.
- We should avoid language that guarantees a migration timeline (we can commit to cooperation, not guaranteed completion dates).
- Add a short clause about auto‑renew: if neither party provides notice by the applicable notice deadline, the Order Form auto‑renews for the same term unless pricing materially changes; include a good‑faith notification requirement 90 days before renewal for any price increase.

If Acme confirms 60 days and accepts the limited transition scope, Legal is comfortable with the addendum as a negotiated exception to the standard Order Form. If Acme insists on broader obligations (e.g., hands‑on migration assistance or financial credits), we need to escalate for exec approval.

Ben — happy to join a 30‑minute call with Acme counsel to walk through the language.

—Neha
Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com

Date: Wed, 9 Sep 2026 15:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood MSA / Order Form — term and cancellation clarification

Ben / Neha — thanks for the quick turnaround and thoughtful options. Acme's procurement team reviewed Option B (60‑day) and the limited transition scope and are comfortable moving forward with the following changes:

- Confirm 60‑day cancellation notice on the Order Form (Option B).
- Keep the limited transition obligations as drafted, but please add a 14‑calendar‑day SLA for Redwood to provide the export package after a termination request (exports may be self‑service; SLA counts calendar days).
- For auto‑renew, we accept the proposed 90‑day price notification but request a 30‑day review window post‑notification before the renewal is final.

If Redwood can accept those three bullets, we will sign the addendum and route to finance for PO issuance. We prefer DocuSign for execution.

Tom — feel free to call out any redline items; otherwise we can proceed.

Appreciate the responsiveness.

Best,
Leah
